auditor_scope: Eight assigned bibliography entries and their uses in paper/sections/01_introduction.tex, paper/sections/02_preliminaries.tex, and paper/appendices/related_work.tex. Independent live primary-source verification. No repository edits.
overall: All eight works exist. No fabricated citation or gross mathematical misattribution found in the checked usages. Metadata completeness and precise version links can be improved. This is a citation audit, not a proof of the research paper's mathematics.

entries.title: Sign-Rank, Index, and List Replicability: Connections and Separations
entries.claim_check: Theorem 1.1 has Ind_Z2(C) <= 2 LR(C)-1 for finite domains. Theorem 1.2 and accompanying discussion identify finite projective-plane incidence matrices, polynomially growing sign-rank, LR <= 3 (Theorem 3.2), and index <= 5. The related-work paragraph matches these statements.
recommended_changes: Keep v1 and use https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18236v1 instead of an unversioned URL.
entries.limits: A v2 dated 2026-07-21 exists. Checked the explicitly cited v1, not a comparative audit of both versions.

entries.title: VALG: An Agentic System for ML Theory Research and Demonstrations on COLT 2026 Open Problems
entries.claim_check: Section 4.3.2 defines the span over seed-averaged outputs for all deterministic complete response rules. Assumption 4.42 states r_A <= B(1+m/tau^2)^k. Under Assumptions 4.39-4.42, Theorem 4.9 constructs a common deterministic representation with pointwise strict margin >= 1-2 epsilon > 1/2. The manuscript correctly calls this conditional and identifies the additional hypothesis.
entries.limits: Keep the current full title: both v2 PDF page 1 and HTML display it. ArXiv landing-page title metadata omits the subtitle. Landing metadata records v2 submission 10 September 2026, while the displayed PDF date is September 11, 2026; the bibliography correctly identifies the arXiv version date.

entries.title: Limitations of Learning Via Embeddings in Euclidean Half Spaces
entries.claim_check: The official abstract studies minimum Euclidean embedding dimension, margin, and low-VC classes requiring large dimension. This supports the manuscript's historical attribution and representation-complexity context. The rank-factorization equivalence is the manuscript's elementary explanation, not an incorrectly attributed numbered theorem.
entries.limits: No DOI needed: the existing official JMLR URL uniquely identifies the work. No claim that this was the first-ever use of every related notion is certified.

entries.title: Approximate is Good Enough: Probabilistic Variants of Dimensional and Margin Complexity
entries.venue: Proceedings of Thirty Third Conference on Learning Theory
entries.claim_check: Definition 2 explicitly distinguishes one embedding law fixed before all distributions and targets from a distribution-dependent law. The former uses expected minimum loss, matching the manuscript's averaged-approximation quantifier discussion. The manuscript explicitly declares its Boolean tie convention and does not silently equate it to degenerate raw-score loss.
recommended_changes: Optionally expand the generic conference name to the official proceedings title.
entries.limits: The paper's reformulated tie rule is an explicit variant; this audit does not independently verify all claimed reductions between variants.

entries.title: On Reductions and Representations of Learning Problems in Euclidean Spaces
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
entries.claim_check: Definitions 13-14 give a single randomized representation before the realizable distribution, with probability of alpha-realizability. Section 8 explicitly distinguishes variants and gives the expected-minimum-loss definition attributed to KMS20. The manuscript's attribution of probabilistic representation ideas is supported.
recommended_changes: Use @inproceedings with the verified venue, pages and DOI; preserve the preprint identifier as a note.
entries.limits: ACM landing page failed in the browser. Exact proceedings metadata was independently obtained from ACM-deposited Crossref data, retained as mid-CMW25-crossref.json. Claims checked against the openly accessible arXiv v1.

entries.title: Efficient noise-tolerant learning from statistical queries
entries.claim_check: The foundational attribution of statistical-query learning is correct. The manuscript uses the standard bounded-expectation formulation of the model. The original journal article's bibliographic data agree exactly with ACM's deposited record and the author's publication list.
entries.limits: ACM page was inaccessible through the browser, but publisher-deposited Crossref metadata was retrieved directly and retained as mid-Kearns98-crossref.json.

entries.title: Evolvability from learning algorithms
entries.venue: Proceedings of the fortieth annual ACM symposium on Theory of computing
entries.claim_check: The author's full version has Theorems 5.2-5.4 characterizing weak CSQ learning and its common low-weight threshold representation. This supports the related-work paragraph's weak-learning context; that paragraph carefully attributes the margin-complexity formulation to the source note rather than quoting a nonexistent Feldman theorem by number.
recommended_changes: Add DOI 10.1145/1374376.1374465 and its DOI URL; optionally expand the proceedings title.
entries.limits: The exact phrase 'margin-complexity characterization' is not the theorem heading in Feldman08; it is a formulation in the source note. Author-hosted full version checked, with proceedings metadata independently verified from ACM-deposited Crossref data retained as mid-Feldman08-crossref.json.

entries.title: Distribution-Independent Evolvability of Linear Threshold Functions
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 24th Annual Conference on Learning Theory
entries.claim_check: Section 3.1, Theorem 8 gives a conjunction CSQ lower bound for error <= 2^(-k/6); Remark 9 extends to randomized learners. Corollary 10 treats growing conjunction size and vanishing target error. The text explicitly says weak distribution-independent CSQ learning of conjunctions is possible. The manuscript correctly distinguishes strong/vanishing-error hardness from weak learning.
recommended_changes: Optionally expand the generic conference name to the official proceedings title.
entries.limits: No gross attribution mismatch found; not an independent reproof of the lower bound.
